title: SS Tibet expedition of 1938

tellings.link_reason: The Nazi/SS expedition to Tibet in the 1930s, the same program as the 1938 SS Tibet expedition.

plain: In 1938 the SS, the Nazi organisation run by Heinrich Himmler, sent an expedition to Tibet. The writer Peter Levenda tells Michels he studied it in captured German documents on microfilm, and he links it to Himmler. The researcher Jason Jorjani mentions it on another episode about Nazi secret projects. He gives no year and says the aim was to get Tibetan scriptures, and he brings in Mount Kailash, a mountain in Tibet. Both tell it as part of a picture of Nazi leaders hunting for old, hidden knowledge, which matters to them because of what that hunt might have turned up.
